title: Koyasan vs Kumano Kodo: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Koyasan for quick, profound visits (1–2 nights); Kumano Kodo for transformative multi-day pilgrimage (4–7 days). Do both if you have time — they share UNESCO World Heritage status as part of the same sacred landscape.

categories.name: Time Required
categories.summary: Koyasan works in 1–2 nights. Kumano Kodo requires 4–7 days of hiking.

categories.name: Physical Difficulty
categories.summary: Koyasan needs no hiking. Kumano Kodo is real multi-day trail hiking.

categories.name: Spiritual Atmosphere
categories.summary: Both are extraordinary — Koyasan is immediate and concentrated; Kumano Kodo is earned over days of forest walking.

categories.name: Cost Per Night
categories.summary: Kumano Kodo minshuku ¥8,500–14,000/person with meals. Koyasan shukubo ¥12,000–20,000.

categories.name: Food Experience
categories.summary: Koyasan's shojin ryori Buddhist vegetarian cuisine is a world-class dining experience.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.summary: Koyasan is 90 min from Osaka by train. Kumano Kodo trailheads require 2.5–3 hrs.

categories.name: Uniqueness
categories.summary: The Kumano Kodo is one of only two pilgrimage trails in the world to hold UNESCO dual designation (with Santiago de Compostela).

categories.name: Best Time
categories.summary: October–November for both. Kumano Kodo avoids rainy season (June–July) and intense summer heat.

faq.question: Should I visit Koyasan or do the Kumano Kodo if I only have time for one?
faq.answer: Koyasan for short trips (2–3 days). Kumano Kodo if you have 5+ days and hiking fitness.

faq.question: Can you combine Koyasan and the Kumano Kodo?
faq.answer: Yes — they're designed as one journey. Do Koyasan first (1–2 nights), then travel to the Nakahechi trailhead for 4–5 days of hiking south.

faq.question: How much does Koyasan temple stay cost?
faq.answer: ¥12,000–20,000 per person per night including shojin ryori dinner and breakfast.
